ctx.x: The second night before we were to arrive in Le Havre, George Johnson and I arrived in the dining room dressed as we always were every night, but to our surprise, the men were dressed in tuxedos. It was gala night which was something that we knew nothing about. So the next night, George and I decided that we would not be caught with out pants down and we came to dinner the last night on board with out tuxedos and to our surprise, no one was wearing tuxedos, except us. That had not happened on the Conte Grande nor…

It was a beautiful day when we arrived in Paris and Freddie had rooms for us at a hotel called Eden on rue Pigalle. Later, after we had arranged things in our room, Freddie took us to the cafe Lizieur, a place that I had known when I came to Paris in 1933 and lived in the hotel above. We met the drummer that was engaged to play with Freddie's group. His name was William Diemar. I think that Diemar came to Europe in 1927 with a group from Buffalo.

After rehearsing for one week, we opened at the Villa d'Este on rue Areene-Housaaye near the Arc de Triomphe and the great Avenue des Champs Elysees. The pianist was French by the name of Jean Ferrier, the bass was Eugene D'Hellemes. The guitarist was from America and his name was Oscar Aleman.
